claims.text: Setting the environment variable PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
The PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service specifies the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API.
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset, the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN can be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN, so a separate domain and second DNS record for the Terraform-compatible API is not required.
The DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN.

The Pulumi state backend guide for Terraform/OpenTofu uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the domain in the Terraform configuration, the `terraform login`/`tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.
A page exists at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ documenting the Terraform state backend guide.
